stem:
Zaid meets the compact writings 5u and 10(y − 3) in his algebra notebook.

How should he read them before any calculation?

options.text: 5u names an 'omitted multiplication sign' rather than five times u.
5u means 5 + u, because the multiplication idea can be dropped.
5u means 5 × u, and 10(y − 3) means 10 times the whole of (y − 3).
The value is whichever numeral appears first in the writing.

teacher.key_rationale: A numeral written next to a letter means multiplication; brackets apply the factor to the whole grouped expression. Dropping multiplication, renaming the compact form, or grabbing the first digit all misread the notation.
